events.name: Dogo Onsen Honkan
events.desc: National-treasure bathhouse, Japan’s oldest hot-spring hall still in use. Kami-no-Yu downstairs is the simple 60-minute soak. Children 2–11 pay half; under 2 free. Towels extra. Closed one December cleaning day some years; check dogo.jp the morning you go. Price: Kami-no-Yu adult ¥700 / child ¥350.

events.name: DOGO ART Ninagawa
events.desc: Mika Ninagawa with EiM colour the Honkan, Asuka-no-Yu courtyard and the shotengai gate through 28 Feb 2027. Free to walk the street installations after dark (winter lights 17:00–23:00). Bath tickets are separate. Best combined with a Honkan soak. Price: outdoor art free; baths extra.

events.name: Tsubaki lanterns Asuka-no-Yu
events.desc: Camellia lanterns in the annex courtyard, typical late November to early February. You can see the garden lights without bathing. Annex bath is a modern alternative to the Honkan if the queue is long. Price: courtyard viewing free; 1F bath adult about ¥610 on the official tariff.

events.name: Matsuyama Castle keep
events.desc: One of twelve original keeps. Ropeway or chairlift from Shinonome, then a short walk. Dec–Jan keep 9:00–16:30, last entry 16:00. Closed the third Wednesday of December for cleaning. Chairlift stops in rain. Price: keep adult ¥520 / elementary ¥160; ropeway return adult ¥520 / child ¥260.

events.name: New Year at Matsuyama Castle
events.desc: Lion dance, first sunrise, citrus giveaway and New Year games on the plaza. 1 Jan ropeway from 6:00 for dawn. Events cancel or change in rain. Keep ticket still required to enter the tenshu. Confirm the 2027 programme on the castle events page. Price: plaza free; keep and ropeway as usual.

events.name: Botchan Train
events.desc: Replica Meiji steam-style tram, 36 seats, no reservations. Runs Sat, Sun and holidays only. Does not run 30 Dec–3 Jan. Board at Dogo ticket counter. About 20 minutes to Matsuyama-shi Station. Price: adult ¥1,300 / child ¥650 one ride.

events.name: Botchan Karakuri Clock
events.desc: Mechanical Botchan and Madonna figures come out on the hour, 8:00–22:00. From 28 Dec to 5 Jan it runs every 30 minutes. Five minutes, free, in front of the station. Easy while you wait for the train or a bath slot. Price: free.

events.name: Saka no Ue no Kumo Museum
events.desc: Ando museum on the Russo-Japanese War novel, next to the castle ropeway. Closed Mondays and year-end (confirm calendar). 9:00–18:30, last entry 18:00. 60–90 minutes. Price: adult ¥500; 65+ and high school ¥250; junior high and under free.

events.name: Ehime Children's Castle
events.desc: Huge outdoor play park: zip line, adventure stations, indoor corners. Car about 20 min from Dogo. Closed Mondays and 29 Dec–1 Jan; open 28 Dec. Festa Luce 2026–27 dates were not posted yet. Price: grounds plus each ride; zip line from about ¥1,400 child.

events.name: Tobe Zoo
events.desc: Ehime’s big zoo: polar bear Peace, elephants, walk-through habitats. 9:00–17:00, last entry 16:30. Closed Mondays and 29 Dec–1 Jan; 2 Jan reopens. 15 min drive from Matsuyama. Feeding hides some animals after 15:30. Price: adult ¥510; high school ¥200; under junior high often free.

events.name: Ehime Science Museum
events.desc: Dinosaurs, industry halls and a 30 m planetarium. About 1 hour by car from Matsuyama. Closed Mondays and 29 Dec–1 Jan. Planetarium is extra and can sell out. Strong indoor day if it rains. Price: permanent adult ¥580, elementary/junior free; planetarium adult ¥580 / child ¥300.

events.name: Imabari Towel Museum
events.desc: Towel-making machines, garden and shop; paid gallery only. About 40 min by car. A Snoopy towel show was listed in 2026 — check the news page for January dates. January has a few closed days some years. Price: grounds free; gallery adult ¥1,000 / junior-senior high ¥800 / elementary ¥600.

events.name: Shimanami rental bikes
events.desc: Official Shimanami Japan rentals next to Sunrise Itoyama. Kids bikes, child seats and e-assist. Winter desk 8:00–18:00. Do a short out-and-back on Kurushima Bridge, not the full 70 km, with a 10-year-old. Book on the rental page. Price: city cycle from about ¥1,000 a day; e-bike more.

events.name: Kurushima Kaikyo Bridge
events.desc: Triple suspension bridge; cycle or walk the separate bike path from Sunrise Itoyama. About 6 km out and back. Wind is raw in December. Closed if wind exceeds 15 m/s. Price: walking free; bikes free until 31 Mar 2028.

events.name: Ishite-ji Temple
events.desc: Shikoku pilgrimage temple 51, five-minute drive from Dogo. Niomon gate is a national treasure. Short hatsumode stop on 1–3 Jan. Grounds stay open; halls may pause at lunch. Price: grounds free; treasure hall adult ¥200.

events.name: Dogo shopping street
events.desc: Covered lane from the station to the Honkan: Botchan dango, tarts, foot-bath side streets. Many shops close 31 Dec afternoon and reopen 2 or 3 Jan. Easy snack walk with a child. Price: street free; dango and tarts about ¥200–¥600.

events.name: Ozu Castle
events.desc: Rebuilt keep you can sleep in (booked months ahead) or just climb. About 50 min drive. Confirm 29 Dec–3 Jan hours on the castle site before you go. Pair with Uchiko on the same loop. Price: keep adult about ¥550; child less.

events.name: Uchiko Yokaichi
events.desc: Wax-merchant street of white-wall houses, 15 min from Ozu. Uchiko-za kabuki theatre is closed for multi-year repair. Quiet in winter; shops may shut 31 Dec–3 Jan. Price: street free; house museums a few hundred yen each.

events.name: Oyamazumi Shrine
events.desc: Island shrine of sea and war gods, huge camphor trees, national-treasure armour in the museum. 70 min drive via Shimanami. Museum has its own ticket. Strong New Year shrine if you want a day out with the car. Price: grounds free; treasure hall adult about ¥1,000.

events.name: Imabari Castle
events.desc: Seawater-moat castle next to the port. Keep museum and wall walk. Closed 29–31 Dec only; park stays open. Easy with Towel Museum the same day. Price: keep adult ¥520; under 18 free.

events.name: Kururin Ferris wheel
events.desc: Iyotetsu Takashimaya roof wheel, 15-minute loop over the castle and the station. 10:00–21:00, last boarding 20:45. Follows store holidays. Under elementary free with an adult. A Botchan Train ticket cuts the standard gondola to ¥500. Price: standard ¥1,000; see-through floor ¥1,500.

events.name: Itoyama Park lookout
events.desc: Free observation deck a few minutes uphill from the Sunrise Itoyama cycling terminal, looking down on Kurushima Kaikyo Bridge and the strait shipping lanes. Bridge floodlighting only runs on set nights; check before an evening trip. Easy add-on before or after the bike ride. Price: free; 90 free parking spaces.

events.name: Bansuisou mansion
events.desc: French-style 1922 villa built for the old Matsuyama clan lord’s descendant, a national important cultural property near the castle ropeway base. 9:00–18:00, closed Mondays unless a holiday. A special exhibition can raise the price through autumn; confirm the December rate. Price: adult normally ¥400 / child ¥200.

events.name: Shionome Kamaboko jako-ten
events.desc: Additive-free jako-ten fish-cake maker with a shop counter by Matsuyama’s central produce market, a short drive from Dogo or the castle. Open daily 9:00–19:00 with irregular closures; a quick call ahead helps. Good for a snack stop, not a sit-down meal. Price: pieces roughly ¥150–¥300 each.

events.name: P・SPO Pig Cafe
events.desc: Micro-pig cafe on the Gintengai covered arcade, opened July 2026, with the pigs out for petting during a timed slot. 10:00–19:00, last entry 18:20. Easy to combine with Kururin or Dogo shopping street the same day. Price: adult ¥1,000 / elementary ¥500 / preschool free per 30 minutes.

events.name: Isaniwa Shrine hatsumode
events.desc: Hachiman shrine on a steep stone stairway just behind Dogo, a national important cultural property and Matsuyama’s main New Year shrine visit. The shrine’s own calendar lists Saitansai (New Year’s rite) on 1 Jan, no hours published for it. Standing office hours: prayers/stamps 9:00–17:00, amulets 9:00–18:00. Expect a queue on the stairs. Price: free.

events.name: Nomauma Highland
events.desc: Free hillside park for Japan’s smallest native horse, the Noma-uma, grazing in open paddocks. Small-animal corner (rabbits, guinea pigs) for petting on weekends and holidays, plus short pony rides. Closed Tuesdays and New Year; confirm dates first. Price: entry free; pony ride about ¥200 a lap.

events.name: Tobe-yaki pottery experience
events.desc: Official Tobe-yaki pottery hall next to Tobe Zoo: painting a blue-and-white piece needs no booking; hand-building or wheel-throwing must be reserved by phone ahead. Hand-building suits a 10-year-old; wheel-throwing is trickier but doable with help. Easy pairing with the zoo. Price: painting and other courses vary by piece.

events.name: Aoshima cat island ferry
events.desc: Small island where free-roaming cats outnumber the handful of residents. Only reachable by the tiny public ferry from Nagahama port, two round trips a day (8:00, 14:30), 34-passenger limit, cancels in rough seas. No shops on the island — bring food and drinks. Combine with Ozu Castle and Uchiko. Price: adult ¥700 / child ¥350 one way.

events.name: Round1 Matsuyama
events.desc: Bowling, karaoke and a large arcade floor (Spocha amusement pass) under one roof, open into the early hours most nights. Good rainy-evening option or after-dinner stop with a 10-year-old. Free parking for 200 cars. Price: arcade pay-per-play or Spocha time-based pass, varies by time block.

events.name: Uwajima bullfighting New Year tournament
events.desc: Togyu, Uwajima’s bull-versus-bull sumo-style bouts in a domed arena above the station — the New Year tournament is confirmed for 2 Jan 2027. Doors 10:00, bouts run about 12:00–14:00. About 1.5–2 hours’ drive from Matsuyama; combine with the castle and a tai-meshi lunch. Price: adult/high school ¥3,000; middle school and under free.

events.name: Uwajima Castle
events.desc: One of Japan’s twelve original castle keeps, small and unrestored, on a hill above the city with bay views. Nov–Feb keep hours 9:00–16:00; free grounds open 6:00–17:00. Easy same-day pairing with the bullring and tai-meshi. Price: keep adult ¥200; high school and under free; 65+ ¥160.

events.name: Kadoya tai-meshi
events.desc: Three-minute walk from Uwajima Station, the local specialty is tai-meshi: raw sea bream, egg and sesame sauce mixed tableside over rice. Set courses run ¥6,000–8,000; lunch is the easier family option. Open year-round except 31 Dec–1 Jan. Good lunch stop on the bullfighting/castle day. Price: courses ¥6,000–¥8,000.

events.name: Windom Farm alpacas
events.desc: Alpaca feeding and petting on a mountain farm about 50 minutes from Matsuyama, walk-in on weekends and holidays 13:30–15:00, other times by reservation only. Ponies and riding also on site. Winter can bring snow and shorter hours; check before driving up. Price: about ¥1,200 per person for 10 minutes with feed.

events.name: Mount Ishizuchi Ropeway
events.desc: Ropeway up Shikoku’s highest mountain, running through December at normal hours and opening at 4:00 on 1 Jan for first-sunrise viewing from the top station. About 1 hour from Matsuyama; cold and possibly icy at the top, dress warmly. Price: round trip adult ¥2,200 / child ¥1,100.

events.name: Ritsurin Garden
events.desc: Daimyo strolling garden with ponds, pine-covered hills and a boat ride, about 2 hours from Matsuyama. December hours 7:00–17:00; free entry on 1 Jan. Combine with Shikoku Mura or Kotohira-gu the same day. Price: adult ¥500 / elementary–junior high ¥170, free 1 Jan.

events.name: Kotohira-gu (Konpira-san)
events.desc: Maritime shrine reached by 785 stone steps (1,368 to the inner shrine) lined with shops — a fun climb for a 10-year-old. Grounds free; the Treasure Hall and Yuichi Gallery open free on weekends/holidays and 30 Dec–3 Jan, otherwise closed. Pair with udon nearby. Price: shrine free.

events.name: Shikoku Mura open-air museum
events.desc: Traditional houses and structures relocated from across Shikoku into a walkable hillside village, plus a Tadao Ando gallery. 9:30–17:00, last entry 16:30, closed Tuesdays. Good hands-on history stop near Takamatsu. Price: adult ¥1,600; junior/high school ¥600; elementary and under free.

events.name: Nakano Udon School
events.desc: Hands-on Sanuki udon class: knead, stomp, roll and cut your own noodles, then eat them, in a lively 40–60 minute session. Reservation required (2+ people), accepted 9:30–14:30. Fun, active alternative to a normal lunch stop in Takamatsu. Price: about ¥1,600 per person.

events.name: Chichu Art Museum, Naoshima
events.desc: Tadao Ando’s mostly-underground museum built around Monet water-lily paintings and James Turrell light installations — open all through our window (a longer closure only starts 12 Jan). Timed online reservation required; quiet, dim rooms suit a curious 10-year-old better than a restless one. Reach via ferry from Takamatsu port. Price: adult ¥2,500–¥3,000 online.

events.name: Naruto whirlpools — Uzu no Michi
events.desc: Glass-floored walkway 45 m above the Naruto Strait, looking down on one of the world’s largest tidal whirlpools — exciting and safe for kids. Time the visit to the tide table on the site for the strongest swirls. 9:00–17:00, last entry 16:30. About 2.5–3 hours from Matsuyama. Price: adult ¥510 / elementary ¥260.

events.name: Awa Odori Kaikan
events.desc: Live Awa Odori dance shows (daytime 11:00/14:00/15:00/16:00, evening 20:00) with a costume/history museum attached, near JR Tokushima Station. Closed 28 Dec–1 Jan, so only fits the start or end of the trip. Pair with the Naruto whirlpools the same day. Price: daytime adult ¥1,300 / child ¥700; museum ¥500 / ¥300.

events.name: Kochi Castle
events.desc: One of Japan’s twelve original castle keeps, with the lord’s residence and palace also intact — rare combination. 9:00–17:00, last entry 16:30, closed 26 Dec–1 Jan. About 2–2.5 hours from Matsuyama; pair with Katsurahama the same day. Price: adult ¥500; under 18 free.

events.name: Katsurahama Aquarium
events.desc: Small, easy aquarium right on Katsurahama Beach: sea turtles, penguins and touch/feeding moments, less overwhelming than a big city aquarium. 9:00–17:00, open daily except 1 Jan. Combine with the beach’s pebble-hunting and the Ryoma statue. Price: adult ¥1,600 / elementary–junior high ¥600 / age 3+ ¥400.

events.name: Marugame Castle Road Reborn
events.desc: Confirmed 2026–27 season (3 Oct 2026–7 Feb 2027): family-crest projections on the castle’s stone walls and cut-paper art on the great gate, plus lit-up station and shopping streets. Free to walk. Castle road lights 17:00–21:00, station front to 22:00, shopping street to 23:00. About 2 hours from Matsuyama. Price: free.

events.name: Kochi Sunday Market
events.desc: Open-air street market running since 1690, about 300 stalls over 1 km near the castle: produce, ironwork, plants and street food like imo-ten. Every Sunday roughly 6:00–14:00, closed only 1–2 Jan — runs on 20, 27 Dec and 3 Jan during the trip. Easy pairing with Kochi Castle. Price: free to browse; food priced individually.

events.name: Ishite-ji New Year’s Eve lanterns
events.desc: Mantō-e, the temple’s annual New Year’s Eve lantern ceremony (世界平和万灯会): candles lit across the grounds from 23:00, running into the midnight bell and the first hatsumode crowds. A recurring yearly tradition tied to the calendar date, though exact 2026 timing should be confirmed closer to the visit. Cold night out, dress warmly. Price: free.

events.name: Otsuka Museum of Art
events.desc: About 1,000 world-famous paintings (Sistine Chapel ceiling, Mona Lisa, Monet’s Water Lilies) reproduced full-size on ceramic panels — huge and touchable, unlike a normal art museum. 9:30–17:00, last ticket 16:00, closed Mondays plus some January dates. Combine with the whirlpools nearby. Price: adult ¥3,300; elementary–high school ¥550.

events.name: Naruto German House
events.desc: Small museum on the WWI German POW camp at Bando, where prisoners and locals lived unusually well together and gave Japan’s first performance of Beethoven’s Ninth Symphony. Dioramas, documents and a robot-theatre show. 9:30–17:00, closed the 4th Monday each month and 28–31 Dec. Price: adult ¥400; elementary–junior high ¥100.

events.name: Hirome Market
events.desc: Indoor food hall a short walk from Kochi Castle: dozens of stalls around shared tables, the local thing to try is katsuo no tataki (seared bonito, flame-torched at the counter). Casual and easy with a 10-year-old — pick a few small plates each. Mon–Sat 10:00–23:00, Sun from 9:00. Price: free entry; dishes individually priced.

events.name: Noichi Zoological Park
events.desc: About 100 species in natural-style habitats, calmer and less crowded than a big-city zoo, roughly 20 minutes from central Kochi. 9:30–17:00, last entry 16:00, closed Mondays and 29 Dec–1 Jan. Free parking. Easy pairing with Kochi Castle or Hirome Market the same day. Price: adult ¥470; under 18 free.

events.name: Sakamoto Ryoma Memorial Museum
events.desc: Hillside museum above Katsurahama Beach on the life of Sakamoto Ryoma, the Bakumatsu-era figure whose statue overlooks the beach below, with ocean views from the building. English audio guide available. 9:00–17:00, last entry 16:30, open every day. Pair with the beach and aquarium. Price: adult ¥500 (¥900 during special exhibitions); high school and under free.

events.name: Kashima deer island
events.desc: Tiny island 300m off Hojo with wild deer roaming freely near the shrine and paths, plus a short climb for sea views. Winter ferry every 30 min, 7:00–19:00 (last from the island), can pause in high wind. Pair with Shiraishi-no-Hana the same trip up the coast. Price: round trip adult ¥230 / child ¥120.

events.name: Shiraishi-no-Hana stones
events.desc: Cluster of huge granite boulders on the shore, nicknamed “Iyo’s Stonehenge”: sunset light lines up through a stone gap at the equinoxes, and through the “turtle stone” around the winter solstice (roughly 21–22 Dec, inside the trip). Small roadside pull-off, no real parking lot. Easy pairing with Kashima. Price: free.

events.name: Sotodomari stone-wall village
events.desc: Small fishing hamlet on a steep bay where houses are wrapped in stone walls built up to the eaves against typhoons — one of Japan’s official “most beautiful villages.” Narrow stone-lined lanes to wander, sea and hill views, free parking by the community hall. About 1h45 south of Matsuyama, furthest point on the trip. Price: free.

events.name: Doi House thatched farmhouse
events.desc: One of Shikoku’s largest thatched-roof farmhouses, an 1827 village headman’s residence with huge timber beams, free to walk through. 9:00–17:00, closed Mondays and the New Year break. Quiet stop about 50 minutes from Matsuyama; pair with the Uwa Folklore Museum nearby. Price: free to view; overnight stays bookable separately.

events.name: Uwa Folklore Museum
events.desc: Packed, slightly chaotic collection of old everyday tools, toys and festival gear from the Uwa area, including local ox-demon (ushi-oni) festival costumes — a fun rummage rather than a formal museum. 9:00–17:00, last entry 16:30, closed Mondays and 29 Dec–3 Jan. Ticket also covers the Meiji-era Kaimei School next door. Price: adult ¥700; student ¥420; younger free.

events.name: Mine Topia Besshi
events.desc: Old copper-mine site turned family park: a mine railway and walk-through tunnels showing the old workings, plus a gold-panning pool that’s a reliable hit with a 10-year-old. Hot-spring bath on site if you want to linger. 9:00–18:00 year-round (closed one week in Feb). Pair with the Science Museum nearby. Price: railway+tunnel about ¥1,300 adult / ¥700 child; gold panning about ¥650 / ¥550.

events.name: Iwagi-jima island
events.desc: Small citrus-terraced island reached by foot-passenger boat from Imabari (~50 min, ¥220 adult / ¥110 child one-way, no cars carried). Mt Sekizenzan viewpoint is 20 min by taxi or a 2-hour walk; the free Edo-period merchant house museum (5 min walk) is closed Tuesdays, holidays and the New Year break. Best done early in the trip — ferries thin out 29 Dec–4 Jan. Price: ferry as above; sights free.
